characterization_methods: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy
evidence: Thickness measurements were carried out by X-ray reﬂection analysis (XRR, Philips PW1880) and spectroscopic ellipsometry (KLA Tencor UV1250). Transmission electron microscopy(TEM, Philips CM300). Rutherford back scattering (RBS) analysis was used to determine the total yield of deposited ZrO2. Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) was used to determine the total yield of Al2O3. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was used to determine the growth of the interfacial oxide. XRD analysis shows that all stacks are amorphous. The k-value dependence as function of the ZrO2 fraction is shown for the mixed oxides and laminates. XRD of thick laminated samples 18-3B and 19-4B show that stacks are amorphous. XRD of thick mixed oxide samples after consecutive anneals during 30 min showing the crystallization above 900 /C176C. C–V-measurements of laminated stacks of Al2O3 and ZrO2 have shown very low leakage currents with respect to their EOT. The C–V-measurements of laminated stacks of Al2O3 and ZrO2 have shown very low leakage currents with respect to their EOT. The k-value of the nanolaminated and mixed oxide stacks varies almost linearly as function of the ZrO2 content. XRD indicated that upon using a nanolaminate or mixed oxide approach the crystallization temperature is dramatically increased. C–V-measurements of laminated stacks of Al2O3 and ZrO2 have shown very low leakage currents with respect to their EOT. These sandwiched dielectric films have shown EOTs as low as 1.1 nm with a leakage current one million times lower than a corresponding SiO2 film.
